newsitem.title: USA: Federal prosecutors subpoena EMLICO papers -- source.
newsitem.headline: Federal prosecutors subpoena EMLICO papers -- source.

text.p: Federal prosecutors have subpoenaed documents in connection with insolvent Electric Mutual Liability Insurance Co's (EMLICO) move last year to Bermuda, a person familiar with the situation said.
The U.S. attorney's office in Boston last week delivered a subpoena to an EMLICO reinsurer demanding information about EMLICO's redomestication, the source said.
The U.S. attorney's office in Boston declined to comment.

The subpoena specifically seeks copies of a 1994 memo prepared by the London law firm Clifford Chance & Co and documents prepared by Chadbourne & Parke, outside counsel for EMLICO, General Electric Co's liability insurer, the source said.

The Clifford Chance memo was reported in the trade press to discuss the advantages of a move to Bermuda and the Chadbourne & Parke documents include a flow chart showing what would happen if EMLICO liquidated in Massachusetts, the source said.

Kemper Insurance Co unit Kemper Reinsurance Co, which was served with the subpoena, last week filed a motion with the Massachusetts Appeals Court for permission to comply with the subpoena. Those documents had been placed under a seal earlier in the year.
When asked about the subpoena, a General Electric spokesman said the company does not comment on investigations.
Meanwhile, EMLICO's reinsurers have asked the Massachusetts division of insurance to reconsider its decision in July not to reopen proceedings that allowed EMLICO to relocate.
The insurance division said it was reviewing public comment on the issue, but had not yet decided whether or not to reconsider its earlier decision.

EMLICO's reinsurers, including Kemper Reinsurance, General Re Corp, Allstate Corp and Lloyd's of London, contend that EMLICO deliberately misled Massachusetts insurance regulators about its solvency, allowing it to move to Bermuda to take advantage of the island's creditor-friendly regulations.
The move leaves the reinsurers, EMLICO debtors, on the hook for potentially greater sums than they would have been required to pay under Massachusetts law.
But General Electric, EMLICO's sole creditor, has contended those allegations were made by reinsurers in an attempt to avoid their contractual responsibilities.
EMLICO won permission to relocate to Bermuda after a short hearing in June 1995. By October, EMLICO had filed for insolvency with about a $500 million surplus shortfall.

In a related matter, Guaranty Fund Management Services, which runs insolvency funds in several states, including Massachusetts, said it was in talks with General Electric regarding costs related to EMLICO's insolvency.
But, the GE spokesman said before EMLICO's move to Bermuda, General Electric waived any claims it may have had against the insolvency funds.

In another related action, Kemper Reinsurance is scheduled to go before a Bermuda judge for a two week hearing, beginning on October 8, to seek permission to have the court reconsider Bermuda's approval of EMLICO's redomestication.

The redomestication was approved by Bermuda's minister of finance and registrar of companies. Kemper has asked that the court reconsider those approvals, but the request came after a deadline for such actions had passed.
A Bermuda judge in late July ruled that EMLICO could proceed with its liquidation.
